title: Placebo optimization of the presurgical video-EEG long-term monitoring
summary: In clinical trials of epilepsy drugs, improvements in seizure situations also occur in the placebo arm. In this study, we want to examine in an optimal investigation setting, the video-EEG long-term monitoring, whether epileptic seizures can be influenced by a placebo, in this case: accelerated. All patients undergo pre-surgical epilepsy diagnostics, where recording of epileptic seizures is absolutely necessary. The patients who were randomly assigned to the "seizure pill" study condition receive a placebo in the morning and evening with the indication that it may accelerate the occurrence of epileptic seizures, so that the video-EEG long-term monitoring can be concluded more quickly. Patients in the "comfort pill" study condition receive a placebo with the indication that we hope it will improve the subjective well-being in the challenging situation of V-EEG monitoring. The patients in the control group do not receive any pill, but they also fill out all questionnaires and diaries. Our hypothesis is that the occurrence of epileptic seizures cannot be influenced by placebo, unlike subjective well-being, for which we hope for positive placebo effects (compared to the control condition).
conditions: Localization-related (focal)(partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with simple partial seizures
Localization-related (focal)(partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with complex partial seizures

interventions.name: daily intake of a covered placebo (1-0-1) associated with the information of an expected possible seizure facilitating effect (i.e. accelerated incidence of an epileptic seizures and, therefore, shortened V-EEG monitoring)
daily intake of a covered placebo (1-0-1) associated with the information of an expected possible improved subjektiv well-being during the demanding V-EEG monitoring
participation in the study (i.e. filling-in all questionnaires etc.), but no intake of specific study medication

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
medical indication for mandatory seizure recording via video-EEG long-term monitoring in the context of presurgical epilepsy diagnosis (implies all exclusion criteria for V-EEG)
Exclusion criteria:
- lack of informed consent or respective capability to provide consent
- patient has a legal guardian
- known allergy for ingredient of placebo pill
Of note, comorbid dissociative non-epileptic seizures are no exclusion criterion.
